# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if any code path returns an error the
model does not sanction.

## index

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HK-18` | `build` | A release record always carries the fields a client reads: the repository, the revision, every file with its path, size and git blob address, and the sources that hold it |
| `HK-20` | `build` | A release record names where its own bytes come from, and the edge sends a client to that same place, so a reader who is not the edge can fetch and check a file without knowing which hub built the record |
| `HK-21` | `build` | A swarm catalog row is filed under the shard key the page resolves a query with, and says it is a listing rather than a checked record, so a search reads one shard and what it draws is not mistaken for proof |
| `HK-23` | `build` | A suggestion the header offers is filed under the words the page resolves a query with, and a panel the head of the catalogue could not fill says so and is completed from the full index, so a short list is never mistaken for the whole answer |
| `HK-24` | `build` | Every row in the UOR address index carries a canonical address and the canonical-form version that minted it, taken here from bytes this build streamed rather than copied from any host, and is filed under the shard key the page resolves a model with |
| `HK-25` | `build` | The page shows a tensor address as checked only when the kernel accepted bytes the page fetched itself, so an address the hub published is never drawn as proof of bytes nobody read |
| `HK-26` | `build` | A filter the panel offers is one whatever is driving the list can act on, so a control is never drawn that cannot narrow anything |
| `HK-29` | `build` | The index learns which other sources hold a release only from the holders record this repository carries, and only for the revision that record names, so a build reads no other hub |
| `HK-35` | `build` | Every safetensors file in the UOR address index is addressed by uor-addr's safetensors realization, and each of its tensors carries the BLAKE3 leaf the file's label binds, which is its address, and the byte range that leaf was taken over, so a reader checks one tensor from a ranged read |

| `HK-01` | `build` | A missing repository and a private repository get the same answer: repository not found, with no source and no ETag |

| `HK-09` | `build` | A commit prefix resolves only when it is 7 to 40 characters long and matches the release's commit |
| `HK-10` | `build` | Received bytes are delivered exactly when their digest and size equal the expected digest and size |
| `HK-11` | `build` | Every header item and every link that stays in the hub opens a screen the kernel renders |
| `HK-12` | `build` | A Hugging Face tool sees no HTTP error exactly when the kernel delivers, and every refusal reaches it as a 4xx or 5xx status with a named error code, except the refusal of a client with no token, which carries exactly the headers Hugging Face sends it |

| `HK-14` | `build` | A model page says Witnessed or Published only when every signature check passed, says Published only for a publisher's signature from the namespace owner, and never shows a witness's signature as a publisher's |

| `HK-19` | `build` | A source that is not vetted is chosen only for a file whose address the record names, so bytes from an untrusted source are always checkable before they are served |
| `HK-22` | `build` | A source nobody vetted is chosen only for a file the release itself addressed, so the party serving the bytes is never the only party that named them; what the ETag says and what the sources may serve are decided by different facts |

| `HK-41` | `build` | A stored piece that matches a piece table of the requested address is always reused and never fetched again |
| `HK-42` | `build` | A piece is refused only when no source is left, and retried only while a source remains |
